chunk_map.heading: Exercise: Write what good means (title + lede)
Phase 2: Run the judge once, then the loop

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 'It lives at `judges/groundedness-judge.md`' comes closest; 'It' binds to 'the check you kept' in the same sentence. L27 'those lines' binds to the lines named L17-21; L65 'your post-it' is named L49 in the prior chunk; 'the loop' (L11) is lede-earned spine vocabulary; 'your judge' (L39) binds to the L7 check. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.

L7 'On Day 2 the check you kept caught claims nobody had made' comes closest; it names the source by claim and path in the same sentence, a schedule day not a deck position. No 'the opening lecture' style pointers; grep 'opening|earlier lecture|the lecture' on body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 'the check you kept' resolves: apt101-catch-it-making-things-up.md L88-90 produces judges/groundedness-judge.md. L27 'Day 1 digests' and L39 'the outcome you picked on Day 2 in ./crux.md' resolve: apt101-pick-the-outcome.md L29 writes ./crux.md; learn-faster-than-the-market.md L20-22 shows the Day 1 digest and Day 2 beats. No dead reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo in the body. Closest: L49 post-it prediction ('you predict the looped digest will fail') precedes the reveal at L59-65, so guess precedes outcome. L45 'A heavy run: ...' is verbless but a warning, not a demo scene.
Closest: chunk 3 (L51-65) is the shortest but carries an instruction, a push-back paragraph and a close. Each chunk holds a self-carrying instruction set; no wait-state-only slide.

chunk 2 L33 'Run the judge once, then the loop' matches L37-47 (hand run, then loop); chunk 3 L51 'See what it missed' matches L55-65; chunk 1 L13 'Write the team's lines' matches L17-31. No contradiction.

Closest: L19 'A quote is a quote, not a paraphrase.' single contrast, not 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'. L7 'stays fixed. It does not move' / L43 'The judge never moves' are restatements across different chunks, not an anaphora triple within a chunk. L45 and L59 'If ... If ...' are pairs. No self-grading superlative, number+retraction, abstraction stack or empty verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L37 'the calibration, step zero' and L7 'floor/ceiling'; both glossed in-line (L7-9, L37) and ordinary engineering vocabulary. grep -nE '\b(beat|compendium|firing|mood|surface)\b' on body -> 0; view greps CLEAN.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 L17 '**The product owner drives**' plus L19-21 bolded role leads = 4 bolds on one slide, over the nominal 1. Harm (bold diluted so nothing stands out) is weak: role names are checklist-item labels each <=5 words, and the same driver-cue shape sits in apt101-five-users L48, apt101-map-the-story L27, apt101-take-it-to-the-team L11 (sibling is the answer). Chunk 0 '**Time:**'/'**What you do:**' are template labels.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: learn-faster-than-the-market.md L29 '[Exercise: Write what good means](exercises/apt101-write-what-good-means.md)' is a standalone include; body view slide_count=3 under the exercise wrapper.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/exercises/apt101-write-what-good-means.md -> 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.'; headers L13/L33/L51 are Phase 1,2,3 consecutive; prose 'step zero' L37 is glossed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/apt101-write-what-good-means.md -> 'slides: 3 ... oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headings L13 'Phase 1: Write the team's lines', L33 'Phase 2: Run the judge once, then the loop', L51 'Phase 3: See what it missed' are phase labels; no law/consolidation slide owes a declarative heading.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 3 L65 'A yardstick you rewrite mid-run is not a yardstick.' is an aphorism kicker (class c), but it gives the reason the judge stays fixed, which L7/L43 state only as fact, and the maintainer Frameworks line 80 names the closing line of Phase 3 as the deliberate in-room Goodhart instance (attested). Stays inside; offered as suggestion only.
